title: Oscar and the Escarpment
premise: Noor Crane, a disgraced railroad engineer carrying a map of closed lines and her late father's debts, is hired to resupply an expedition surveying a route through the escarpment upriver. When the expedition's radio goes silent, Noor teams with Oscar, a river pilot whose family was displaced when the lines were closed, and together they push into monsoon country to find out why. They discover the expedition leader faked his disappearance to bury evidence that the closed line was sabotaged for profit, framing Oscar's father years ago. In the climax, as the monsoon peaks, Noor and Oscar expose the sabotage logbook and bring the survivors downriver, choosing justice outside the courts; Noor burns her father's debt papers, and Oscar takes his father's name back at last.
about_author: Orsen Winterbourne is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping river routes across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: POV Noor. In a rain-soaked rail town, Noor Crane accepts a contract to resupply the Halloway expedition upriver, hiding the fact that she's fleeing creditors and a ruined reputation. Her father's old compass points not north but toward a line on her map marked CLOSED. Emotional beat: restless hope disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: A Pilot Named Oscar
chapters.summary: POV Noor. At the docks she hires the only boat willing to run the escarpment in season: Oscar Vane, taciturn, half-feral, who refuses payment and asks instead that she look for someone lost upriver years ago. Their first argument over the route reveals he knows the water better than any chart. Emotional beat: wary friction becoming grudging respect.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Two days upriver, the expedition's scheduled check-in never comes. Oscar hears it first: static where a voice should be. A storm front builds behind them, and Noor insists they press on while Oscar warns the river will close like a trap. Emotional beat: dread settling in as the forest thickens and the current quickens.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. They find the expedition's abandoned forward camp: supplies intact, a torn tent, and a radio smashed from inside, not outside. Oscar recognizes boot prints leading toward the old closed rail tunnel, a place his father was blamed for destroying. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Following the disused service road along the cliff face, Noor reads the terrain like her father taught her and realizes the 'collapse' that closed the line was engineered, cut supports, not rotten ones. The debt she carries was built on this lie. Emotional beat: fury at discovering her inheritance is complicity.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The monsoon breaks early and hard. The boat tears open on submerged debris; they shelter in a culvert with two expedition survivors, a young surveyor named Ilsa and a wounded foreman, who reveal leader Edmund Halloway staged the disappearance himself. Emotional beat: terror giving way to resolve, strangers becoming a crew.

chapters.title: Hollow Signal
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Using the wrecked radio's battery, Noor sends a false all-clear to lure Halloway's supply launch upstream, splitting his party. Oscar slips through flooded forest to mark their position, confronting the place his father died. Emotional beat: courage sharpened by personal reckoning.

chapters.title: The Logbook
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. In Halloway's base camp above the tunnel mouth, Oscar finds the original inspection log proving the sabotage and the payoff trail that framed his father. Halloway catches him; Noor arrives in the flood's worst hour, and the standoff turns physical as the river rises through the camp. Emotional beat: the climax, everything risked at once.

chapters.title: High Water Justice
chapters.summary: POV Noor. With the camp flooding, Noor radios the evidence to every station on the band, letting the whole valley hear Halloway's confession extracted by Ilsa. Halloway, refusing rescue, is swept away clutching his contracts; the others are pulled aboard the patched boat. Emotional beat: catharsis, justice delivered by witness rather than verdict.

chapters.title: Open Lines
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Weeks later, the river drops. The reopened inquiry vindicates Oscar's father; Noor burns her debt papers on the dock and signs on to survey the line's restoration, with Oscar as her pilot. The compass finally points somewhere true. Emotional beat: quiet arrival, identity reclaimed and futures opened.
